auth.description: Google OAuth2 access token sent as a bearer; short-lived, and refreshed by the host rather than by generated Flux
auth.name: google.access_token
auth.subject: unstated

description: Google Workspace: read and send Gmail messages, read and create Calendar events, read and rename Drive files

operations.description: Get one Gmail message by id, in Gmail's default `full` format: headers plus the parsed MIME structure, whose body parts are base64url-encoded. Needs the `gmail.readonly` scope (or `gmail.modify`)

params.description: The mailbox to read: the literal `me` for the token's own mailbox, or the user's email address. `me` is what a flow should use — an address here must be one the token is authorized for, and domain-wide delegation is the only way that happens
params.name: user_id

params.description: The message's id, the hex string Gmail's own listings and its `X-GM-MSGID` header report. It is not the RFC 2822 `Message-ID`
params.name: message_id

historyId.description: The mailbox history id at which this message was last changed. **A string**, despite being an integer value

id.description: The message's id — what this operation takes

internalDate.description: When Gmail received it, as **epoch milliseconds in a string** — not an ISO timestamp, and not seconds. The RFC 2822 `Date` header inside `payload` may differ from it

labelIds.description: The labels applied, as ids: `INBOX`, `UNREAD`, `SENT`, `IMPORTANT`, `CATEGORY_PERSONAL`, plus any user label's opaque id. `UNREAD`'s presence is how read-state is expressed — there is no `read` boolean

payload.description: THE MESSAGE ITSELF, as a MIME tree: `{partId, mimeType, filename, headers, body, parts}`. `headers` is an **array** of `{name, value}` — so `Subject` and `From` are found by searching it, not by keying into it — and each `body.data` is **base64url-encoded**. A multipart message's text is in `parts`, not in the top-level `body`

snippet.description: A short plain-text extract of the body — the only text in this response that needs no decoding, and it is truncated

threadId.description: The conversation it belongs to. Several messages share one

operations.description: Send a Gmail message, supplied as a complete base64url-encoded RFC 2822 message. It is delivered immediately from the token owner's mailbox and cannot be recalled. Needs the `gmail.send` scope

params.description: The sending mailbox: the literal `me` for the token's own mailbox, or an email address the token is authorized to send as
params.name: user_id

params.description: The complete RFC 2822 message, base64url-encoded (`-` and `_` rather than `+` and `/`). Must include at least a `To` header and a body
params.name: raw

id.description: The sent message's id — the only handle on a mail that cannot be recalled, and what `google-gmail-message-get` reads back

labelIds.description: Typically `["SENT"]`. Google documents the response as "an instance of Message" without stating which members are populated on a send, so treat anything beyond `id` and `threadId` as possibly absent

threadId.description: The thread it landed in. Equal to `id` for a new conversation

operations.description: List every label in a mailbox — the system labels (`INBOX`, `SENT`, `SPAM`) and the user's own — as `{"labels": [...]}`. Needs the `gmail.readonly` scope (or `gmail.labels`)

params.description: The mailbox whose labels to list: the literal `me` for the token's own mailbox, or an authorized email address
params.name: user_id

labels.description: Every label in the mailbox, in one unpaginated response — there is no `nextPageToken` on this method. Only the five members below are returned by a *list*; the per-label message counts belong to a `labels.get`

id.description: The label id — `INBOX`, `SENT`, `UNREAD` and the other system labels are ids in their own right; a user label's id is opaque (`Label_12`). This is what appears in a message's `labelIds`

name.description: The display name. A nested label's name carries its path, e.g. `Clients/Acme`

type.description: `system` labels cannot be renamed or deleted

operations.description: Get one calendar event: its summary, start and end, organizer, attendee list and status. Needs the `calendar.events.readonly` scope (or `calendar.readonly`)

params.description: The calendar the event is on: the literal `primary` for the token owner's own calendar, or a calendar address such as `team@group.calendar.google.com`
params.name: calendar_id

params.description: The event's id, as Calendar's own listings report it. A recurring event's single instance carries a `_`-suffixed id (`abc123_20260130T090000Z`)
params.name: event_id

attendees.description: Each `{email, displayName, organizer, self, optional, responseStatus}`, where `responseStatus` is `needsAction`, `declined`, `tentative` or `accepted` — this is how attendance is read. Absent entirely on an event with no attendees, such as every event `google-calendar-event-insert` creates. Personal data: it is a list of named people's addresses

conferenceData.description: The conference in full: `entryPoints` with join URLs and dial-in numbers, plus a `conferenceId`. Contains the same joinable links as `hangoutLink`

creator.description: Same shape; the creator need not still be the organizer

end.description: Same shape, and **exclusive**: an all-day event on the 30th has `end.date` of the 31st. For a recurring event this describes the first instance

etag.description: The resource's ETag, as a quoted string

hangoutLink.description: The Google Meet join link, when the event has a conference. **Anyone holding it can join the meeting**, so treat it as sensitive rather than as an ordinary URL

htmlLink.description: The event's page in Google Calendar — the link to give a human

id.description: The event id — what this operation takes

location.description: Free text, not a structured address

organizer.description: `{email, displayName, self}` — who owns the event. `self` is true when it is the token's own calendar

recurringEventId.description: Present on an instance of a recurring event: the id of the series it belongs to

start.description: WHEN IT STARTS, as an object: `dateTime` (RFC 3339) for a timed event **or** `date` (`yyyy-mm-dd`) for an all-day event — never both — plus an optional IANA `timeZone`. Reading `start.dateTime` unconditionally misses every all-day event

status.description: **A cancelled event is still returned here**, with `cancelled`. Check this before treating the event as live

summary.description: The title. Absent on an event created without one, which Calendar renders as "(No title)"

operations.description: Create a timed event on a calendar. No attendees can be declared yet, so nobody is invited and no notification is sent; invite people in Calendar afterwards. Needs the `calendar.events` scope

params.description: The calendar to create the event on: the literal `primary` for the token owner's own calendar, or a calendar address the token can write to
params.name: calendar_id

params.description: The event's title, as it appears in the calendar grid
params.name: summary

params.description: When the event starts, RFC 3339 **with a UTC offset** — `2026-01-30T09:00:00+01:00` or `2026-01-30T08:00:00Z`. An offset-less value is rejected, because the `timeZone` field that would resolve it is not declarable yet
params.name: start_time

params.description: When the event ends, RFC 3339 with a UTC offset. Must be after `start_time`; Calendar rejects an end that precedes its start
params.name: end_time

attendees.description: ABSENT on every event this operation creates: no attendee can be declared yet (C-56), so nobody was invited and nobody was notified

htmlLink.description: The event's page in Google Calendar — the link to give a human

iCalUID.description: The RFC 5545 UID, which is what identifies this event across calendars — distinct from `id`

id.description: The new event's id — the only handle on it, and what `google-calendar-event-get` reads back

organizer.description: `{email, displayName, self}` — the calendar the event was created on

sequence.description: The iCalendar revision number, `0` on creation

start.description: `{dateTime, timeZone}` as created. Calendar resolves the offset that was sent into its own representation, so this may not be the literal string that was sent

summary.description: Echoes the title that was sent

operations.description: Get one calendar's own metadata — its summary, description, location and time zone. This is the calendar, not its events: use `google-calendar-event-get` for one of those. Needs the `calendar.readonly` scope

params.description: The calendar to read: the literal `primary` for the token owner's own calendar, or a calendar address
params.name: calendar_id

id.description: The calendar's address, e.g. `you@example.com` or `team@group.calendar.google.com`. Asking for `primary` resolves to this

location.description: Free-text geographic location of the calendar

timeZone.description: The calendar's own IANA time zone, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`. **This is what an event's offset should be computed from** — `google-calendar-event-insert` cannot send a `timeZone`, so the caller has to apply the right offset itself

operations.description: Get one Drive file's metadata — its id, name and MIME type. This never returns file content: downloading needs `alt=media`, which is a query parameter and therefore unavailable (C-30). Needs the `drive.metadata.readonly` scope (or `drive.readonly`)

params.description: The file's id — the base64url-ish string in its Drive URL after `/d/`. A folder is a file too, with the folder MIME type
params.name: file_id

operations.description: Rename a Drive file: sets its name and changes nothing else. It does not move, share, trash or replace the file's content. Needs the `drive.file` scope for files this token created, or `drive` for any other

params.description: The file's new name. Drive does not require names to be unique within a folder, so this can collide with a sibling
params.name: name

services.description: Gmail: read a message, send a message, list a mailbox's labels
services.name: gmail

services.description: Google Calendar: read a calendar and its events, create an event
services.name: calendar

services.description: Google Drive: read and rename a file's metadata
services.name: drive
